# How Can I Restore a Previous Version of an Internal App After a Mistake?


You restore a previous version by opening the app's version history and rolling back to a saved point before the mistake was made, rather than trying to manually undo each individual change. On **Jestor** , this runs through native **App Versioning** .


An internal app changed by mistake, with no way to revert to how it worked before, turns a small configuration error into a scramble to manually reconstruct the previous working state.


## What no version history costs


- A configuration mistake turning into a scramble to manually reconstruct the prior state
- Uncertainty about exactly what the app looked like before the unwanted change
- Time spent piecing together a fix instead of simply rolling back
- Hesitation to experiment with changes, for fear of not being able to undo them


## How app version restoration works


- **App Versioning** keeps a history of saved states as the app evolves
- Rolling back restores the app to a previous version directly
- No manual reconstruction of individual changes is needed
- This confidence in reversibility supports more comfortable experimentation


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Version history replaces a manual reconstruction scramble with a direct rollback
- Confidence in reversibility encourages the team to experiment more freely
- Mistakes become quickly recoverable instead of a lasting configuration problem
- This scales from an individual builder's mistake to team-wide app development

## Frequently Asked Questions


**How many previous versions are typically retained?** This depends on your specific plan configuration. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Does restoring a version affect the data inside the app's tables?** Version history primarily covers the app's structure, worth confirming specifics for your case.


**Can I see what changed between two different versions?** Depending on the interface, version history typically shows what changed and when.
